title: The Road to Extraordinary
coreMove: Build a support system that keeps focused practice alive through the long middle after easy gains fade.
sourcePressure: The chapter explains that extraordinary performance grows through a long developmental road with rising standards, deepening commitment, accumulating gains, and real costs. Frozen sidecar for chapter 7 contains no traceable named figure, study, place, date, or artifact beyond the authors and chapter mechanism; sourceAnchors stays empty rather than inventing one.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version turns extraordinary performance into inspirational grit or a single heroic commitment.

hook: sprinter eating cold rice from old Peak draft
examples: young pianist family pressure from old draft
founder sales calls as identity trial

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person 'You' direct address, retrospective 'It took her three weeks to see', question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

exampleSpecs.domain: youth chess club progression from casual games to rated study
exampleSpecs.audience: a parent-coach trying to keep challenge alive without burning children out
exampleSpecs.stakes: promising players quit when early wins end and no support explains the plateau
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Grace replaces Friday free play with one annotated loss, one endgame drill, and a parent ride schedule so practice survives the first losing streak
exampleSpecs.firstImage: score sheets curled beside a locked community-center cabinet

exampleSpecs.audience: a trainee whose early excitement fades after repeated failed assessments
exampleSpecs.stakes: a vital skill stalls unless feedback, rest, and identity are protected through failure
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Matthew lays three failed assessment sheets beside a revised practice calendar and schedules mentor review before the next simulation instead of adding random extra shifts
exampleSpecs.firstImage: three creased assessment sheets under a clear clipboard cover

exampleSpecs.domain: ballet academy recovery plan after growth-related coordination changes
exampleSpecs.audience: a dancer whose body changes faster than her old technique
exampleSpecs.stakes: shame can turn a temporary reorganization into quitting
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Juliette and her teacher lower jump volume, add balance drills, and mark progress weekly so the road continues through awkward months
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a balance board resting beside pointe shoes with loose ribbons

exampleSpecs.domain: elite pastry exam preparation across a winter season
exampleSpecs.audience: a craft learner facing months of tiny technical corrections
exampleSpecs.stakes: she may abandon the exam because ganache tempering gains are invisible week to week
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Marit photographs each split ganache, logs room temperature, and keeps the coach meeting even after two flat weeks so the pattern can accumulate
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a glossy ganache smear cooling on a marble slab

exampleSpecs.domain: community-college robotics team preparing for regional trials
exampleSpecs.audience: a team lead learning that the road needs structure, not only excitement
exampleSpecs.stakes: early prototype wins hide the repair schedule needed for real competition
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Luca predicts the prototype will keep improving from late nights, then the drive chain fails twice; he builds a boring weekly test cycle and parts log that carries the team through the plateau
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a drive chain link snapped beside a plastic parts bin

exampleSpecs.domain: regional theater actor learning dialect work over a full rehearsal run
exampleSpecs.audience: a performer tempted to rely on opening-week adrenaline
exampleSpecs.stakes: the accent decays under emotion unless practice is sustained beyond first confidence
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You watch Adaeze keep a dialect notebook, schedule short coach checks after emotional scenes, and protect vocal rest so the skill survives the whole run
exampleSpecs.firstImage: phonetic notes penciled beside a wrinkled rehearsal call sheet

skillTargets: separate long-term support from raw motivation
identify the long middle and plateau risk
choose structures that preserve practice through costs
evaluate when ambition lacks support design

tryThisNowSpec: Name one skill where early progress has slowed. Write the support that is missing now: coach check, recovery, schedule protection, progress log, peer, or reason to return after a bad week.
